correctness.rationale: Definitions are fixed primitive integral conic and seven lines, with geometric reduced support over algebraic closures at p>=5. An exact integer certificate enumerates all 35 line-triple determinants (five zero; other prime support only 2,3,5), conic determinant 256, all 7 binary line-section discriminants (256, four times 1024, twice 9216), 21 line intersections, 14 conic contacts collapsing to exactly 12 integral projective points, and 66 pairwise cross-content gcds with prime support only 2,3,5. Thus all twelve ordinary points persist distinctly for every p>=7. Complete F5 projective point enumeration and degree-2 Bezout contacts give precisely six ordinary points on five reduced lines plus conic; pairs L3=L5 and L4=L6 are the only line collapses. The determinant -7 and exact pullback matrix identity certify projective equivalence to CL4. The standalone pure-Python verifier reproduced all the cited checks. Limits on p=2,3 and the nonreduced full product at p=5 are explicitly excluded.

value.rationale: The two fixed arrangements are separately distinguished named free objects in a complex classification. The exact arithmetic degeneration of the larger arrangement at a unique admissible prime and its exceptional identification with the smaller one supplies a structural relationship between two constructions, stronger than recomputing a familiar characteristic-zero multiplicity table. The complete all-prime stability theorem answers a natural reduction question, and the explicit projective map is not forced by weak combinatorics. Independent audit is not claimed.
